text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — our GPU savings coverage in us-west-2 dropped to 63% this week, and I’m seeing ~18 orphaned reserved capacity slots tied to old p3 instances. Renewal window for a chunk of our commitments is in 14 days.
Liam O'Connor: Ugh. Do we know if those orphans are from a single team/stack or spread across tenants?
Maria Chen: Spread. Mostly training queues that migrated to p4d last year but reservations were left behind. Quick scan SQL below:
```sql
select instance_type, region, sum(reserved_hours)-sum(used_hours) as orphan_hours
from billing.ri_usage_by_hour
where region='us-west-2' and product_family='GPU'
group by 1,2
order by orphan_hours desc;
```
Maria Chen: That returns p3.8xlarge ~432 orphan_hours last month (aggregate across tags).
Jon Patel: Can we exchange those RIs to p4 or convert to savings plan? What’s AWS window?
Satya Rao: We can exchange convertible RIs across families if purchased as convertible, but not if they were standard RIs. Need to check purchase type. Also Savings Plans would be more flexible but require committing spend level.
Maria Chen: Checked — about 60% are convertible, 40% standard (legacy purchases). Looking at cost delta, converting the convertible portion to a compute savings plan would save ~18% vs current on-demand spend for our baseline workloads.
infra-bot: [alert] Savings coverage change detected: us-west-2 GPU coverage decreased by 22% vs rolling-30d. Affected reservations: 18. See dashboard -> /billing/commitments/2160001234.
Liam O'Connor: For the standard RIs, we could either 1) try to exchange via AWS console for smaller SKUs used by batch, 2) sell on the RI marketplace, or 3) let them expire and push those workloads to dedicated pools + autoscale. Thoughts?
Jon Patel: Marketplace sale adds ops friction and ~5-10% fee. If we can rehome them to lower-utilized non-prod clusters in same region, that might be fastest win. Any candidate clusters?
Maria Chen: Non-prod GPU cluster 'spur-qa' in us-west-2 has ~120 spare hours/day (mostly off-peak). We could migrate nightly heavy jobs there and tag usage to consume RIs before renewal. Quick plan:
- Today: tag all affected instances with "ri-consume:usw2-sweep" so we can track.
- +2 days: schedule nightly batch migration for training jobs to spur-qa.
- +7 days: attempt convertible exchange for remaining convertible RIs.
- +12 days: decide marketplace vs expire for standards.
Satya Rao: Agree. Add a cost-risk row: moving non-prod increases latency for dev runs but saves ~$24k/month. Also check cross-account attachment constraints if we've consolidated billing.
Liam O'Connor: I can push the tag + run the delta query again. Will paste exact CLI we should run: 
```bash
aws ce get-reservation-coverage --time-period Start=$(date -d '30 days ago' +%F),End=$(date +%F) --group-by Key=REGION,Type=DIMENSION
```
Maria Chen: Thx. Also attach this helper SQL to the ops runbook so the oncall can re-run if numbers change.
Jon Patel: If we decide to buy a compute savings plan, we should model break-even for 1yr vs 3yr. 1yr might be flexible enough given growth.
infra-bot: [note] Scheduled check in 48h: rerun orphan-hours query and report to #eng-infra.
Liam O'Connor: I'll run the tag + migrate tests tonight and report back by 2160003000. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: Perfect. If anyone objects to using spur-qa for the sweep, speak up now. Otherwise I'll open the internal ticket and assign follow-ups. :eyes:
Satya Rao: No objections. Please include a quick rollback plan in the ticket for any training jobs that exceed time budget.
Jon Patel: Add a line about potential vendor discount if we commit to 3yr dedicated for steady throughput — sales might negotiate.
Maria Chen: Will do. Opening ticket: INFRA-9876 (ri-orphan-sweep). Assigning @Liam, @Satya. I'll paste all queries and the plan there.
Liam O'Connor: Thanks — will update after tonight's run.
Maria Chen: Closing this thread for now, followups will be in INFRA-9876. :white_check_mark:
